newsitem.title: INDIA: India crude refining capacity to double by 2007.
newsitem.headline: India crude refining capacity to double by 2007.

text.p: India must boost its annual refining capacity by an additional 109 million tonnes over the next decade in order to meet its growing petroleum needs, senior industry officials said on Tuesday.

"An additional refining capacity of 109 million tonnes needs to be established in the next 10 years," S.N. Mathur, chairman of state-run oil refiner IBP Co told an oil and gas conference in the Indian capital.
India's current annual refining capacity is about 61.55 million tonnes. The country has 14 refineries, 13 of which are state-owned.
Industry officials said India's demand for petroleum products is currently growing at an average rate of seven to eight percent per annum.
"In the last few years we have constantly achieved a capacity utilisation of 100 percent or more," Mathur said.
He said the government was keenly trying to formulate policies which could attract foreign investment and also help expand the existing refineries with the lowest cost option.
Energy analysts expect India's demand for petroleum products to rise to 150 million tonnes by the turn of the century from the present 81 million tonnes and to 190 million tonnes by 2010.
More than half of the country's present annual demand is met through imports.
Mathur said the current hydrocarbon loss during refining in Indian refineries was around 0.7 percent to one percent and an "action plan" was being evolved to cut it to 0.5 percent.
Industry officials said India was expected to add an additional annual refining capacity of 70 million tonnes during the ninth five-year plan, which began on April 1, 1997.

"This would require an investment level of approximately $14 billion," Mathur said. An additional $2.8 billion would be needed in the ninth plan to upgrade pollution control techniques including research and development.
R.K Narang, former chairman of state-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) told the conference the refining industry was carrying out upgrades to meet environmental specifications.
"In addition, the oil industry is exploring the possibility of integration with petrochemicals and power," Narang said.
Narang said India's liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) demand, currently 4.2 million tonnes per annum, was expected to grow to 9.5 million tonnes by 2000-2001 and to 13.2 million tonnes by 2006-07.

"Plans have been drawn up by the industry to develop additional infrastructure such as import facilities, additional storage tankers, LPG bottling plants and transportation fleet to meet the future demand," Narang said.
Narang said India had also drawn up plans to increase its crude pipeline network to 11,000 kms in the ninth plan from the present around 7,000 kms.
"This would call for massive investments, where alliance and joint ventures approach is being encouraged," Narang said.
